plan.problem: Git-derived changed paths were previously line/tab parsed and normalized, and after initial M2 remediation downstream Risk/Impact classification still rewrote literal backslashes, allowing distinct repository paths to alias.
plan.currentContract: staging/main still uses non-NUL changed-path parsing and shared path normalization; the superseded PR proved a partial fix but was closed when downstream normalization required files outside its immutable r0 scope.
plan.whyExistingIsInsufficient: Leading-space or quoted names can lose identity in Scope, and a literal root filename such as data\works.js can be rewritten downstream to data/works.js and inherit a known-domain exemption.
plan.design: Use NUL-delimited Git output for changed/untracked paths, keep Git-derived path strings literal in Scope, and make Risk/Impact classification operate on those same literal strings without separator or prefix rewriting.
alternativesRejected: Decode Git C-style quoted line output manually; NUL-delimited output avoids quoting entirely.
Continue normalizing Git-derived paths in downstream policy; this preserves unsafe aliasing.
Extend superseded PR #30 with r1; trusted gates intentionally reject Plan revisions inside the same PR.
plan.compatibility: Ordinary repository paths retain their existing classification. Plan-pattern normalization remains separate from Git path identity.
boundaryCases: Leading-space path must not match the same path without leading space.
Unicode, tab, newline, backslash and quote filenames must survive changed-path collection literally.
Rename and untracked worktree paths must preserve literal names.
Literal root filename data\works.js must remain distinct from data/works.js and receive unknown-code risk/impact treatment.
testPlan: Create temporary real Git repositories containing unusual filenames and assert collectChangedPaths returns exact literal identities.
Assert Scope does not trim or rewrite leading-space/backslash paths.
Assert classifyRiskPath and collectRiskRequirements do not alias data\works.js onto known domain data.
Assert deriveRequiredImpacts requires risk.high-risk-review and runtime.regression for the literal backslash JavaScript path.
Run Change Operations regression suite and trusted Change PR Gate.
plan.promotionRisk: Staging Change OS only. Incorrect path handling could over-allow or falsely reject changes, so trusted gate review and post-fix canary are required.
